--- title: "Responsible Use of AI for Non-Coders: Interface Tour" subtitle: "
Bioinformatics Resource Center - Rockefeller University" author: - "[http://rockefelleruniversity.github.io/responsible_use_of_AI_for_noncoders/](http://rockefelleruniversity.github.io/responsible_use_of_AI_for_noncoders/)" - "[brc@rockefeller.edu](mailto:brc@rockefeller.edu)" --- ::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"} # Responsible Use of AI for Non-Coders: Interface Tour ::: ## Overview *Presenter: ?? — 10 mins* A quick tour of two graphical apps side by side, **Codex** (left) and **Claude Code** (right). The features are largely the same in both. Knowing where they live is what matters. - [Chat vs code](#chat-vs-code) - [Projects](#projects) - [Models and effort](#models) - [Usage](#usage-and-limits) - [Permissions and context](#permissions) - [Seeing what it did](#seeing-what-it-did) ??Timing guide: ~1 min per slide. Slides marked (optional) can be dropped if running over.?? # Interface tour {background-color="#23373B" .center .middle} ## The layout at a glance :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Codex** ??Screenshot: the full Codex window with callouts (numbered 1-5) on: conversation area, prompt box, sidebar (projects/sessions), settings, and where the model is chosen.?? ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Claude Code** ??Screenshot: the full Claude desktop app on the Code tab with the same five callouts, using the same numbering so the audience can compare.?? ::: :::: Talking point: the same parts exist in both. Learn the layout once. ## Chat vs code {#chat-vs-code} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Codex** ??Screenshot: how Codex separates a plain conversation from a coding/agent task (confirm where this lives in the Codex UI).?? ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Claude Code** ??Screenshot: the Chat tab and the Code tab of the Claude desktop app, side by side or tab-switch cropped.?? ::: :::: - **Chat:** you ask, it answers. It cannot touch your files. - **Code / agent:** it reads your files, runs commands and writes files on your computer. - This is the main difference between asking a question and delegating a task, and it's where the risk changes. (Links to *Terminology: model / app / agent* in the Basics section.) ## Projects {#projects} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Codex** ??Screenshot: choosing / adding a project folder in Codex, and the list of past sessions for it.?? ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Claude Code** ??Screenshot: choosing a working folder in the Claude Code tab, and the session list in the sidebar.?? ::: :::: - The agent works inside the **folder you give it**. Choose it deliberately. - Each project has its own sessions (conversations) and, optionally, its own instruction file. (Instruction files are covered in the workflow section.) - Never point it at a folder holding raw data or anything you wouldn't want changed. ## Models {#models} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Codex** ??Screenshot: the model picker open in Codex, showing the available models.?? ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Claude Code** ??Screenshot: the model picker open in Claude Code (Opus / Sonnet / Haiku), ideally with the model name visible near the prompt box.?? ::: :::: - Bigger models are slower, cost more usage, and are usually better at hard, multi-step problems. Smaller models are fast and fine for simple tasks. - Note which model you used: it's part of reproducibility (see the workflow section). ## Effort and thinking :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Codex** ??Screenshot: the effort / reasoning setting in Codex (confirm where it is exposed in the UI).?? ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Claude Code** ??Screenshot: the effort setting in Claude Code, and an example of the thinking display if shown.?? ::: :::: - Higher effort means the model thinks longer before answering. This usually means better answers on hard problems, but slower responses and more usage. - Start low for simple questions, raise it for complex analysis steps. ## Usage and limits {#usage-and-limits} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Codex** ??Screenshot: where Codex shows usage / remaining limit.?? ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Claude Code** ??Screenshot: the usage view in Claude (plan limits, how much is left in the current window).?? ::: :::: - Plans have limits that reset over time. Large models, high effort and long sessions use them up faster. - Rockefeller's Claude for EDU usage limits should be more favorable than the standard plans (see the *AI Strategy at Rockefeller* section). ## Permissions {#permissions} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Codex** ??Screenshot: an approval prompt in Codex (e.g. asking permission to run a command), and where the approval / sandbox mode is set.?? ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Claude Code** ??Screenshot: a permission prompt in Claude Code, and the permission-mode selector.?? ::: :::: - The agent asks before doing certain things. The prompt is a decision point: read it before approving. - Where you set this decides how much the agent can do without asking. (Covered in depth in the *hard lines* part of the workflow section.) ## Giving it context :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Codex** ??Screenshot: attaching a file or referencing a file in the prompt box in Codex.?? ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Claude Code** ??Screenshot: attaching a file / @-mentioning a file in the Claude Code prompt box.?? ::: :::: - The model only knows what is in the conversation. Attach or reference the files it needs. (Links to *What Happens With a Query*.) - Anything you attach is sent to the model. Check the data policy first. ## Seeing what it did {#seeing-what-it-did} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Codex** ??Screenshot: the view of file changes (a diff) and the commands it ran in Codex.?? ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Claude Code** ??Screenshot: the task list, diff view and terminal output in Claude Code after a short task.?? ::: :::: - Review the changes and the commands, not just the final answer. - This is how you keep the code and the record of what ran (see *Reproducibility* in the workflow section). ## Settings that matter for your data (optional) :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Codex** ??Screenshot: the settings page covering data sharing / privacy and memory (confirm what Codex exposes).?? ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Claude Code** ??Screenshot: the privacy / memory / connectors settings in the Claude app.?? ::: :::: - Check what is switched on: memory, connectors and integrations, data-sharing settings. - Defaults differ between personal and institutional accounts. See the *AI Strategy at Rockefeller* section. ## Other features worth a mention (optional) ??Pick any that fit the time: connectors, skills, scheduled tasks, session history/search, running a task in the background, switching between apps.?? ## Summary - The two apps do the same jobs with different layouts. - Choose the **mode** (chat vs code), the **folder**, the **model** and the **effort** deliberately. - Read **permission prompts** and **review what was done**. ??Optional: a live demo of one short task in each app instead of this slide??
